rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' rescue at sea was extraordinary because the basket could have overturned, struck a wall, or been carried by the current into the salt sea or other dangers.
rows.anchor: لتعرضه للغرق بقلب الريح للتابوت , أو بكسره في بعض الجدر أو غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative for the sea to cast the basket ashore asserts the certainty of its rescue, as if the sea understood and obeyed an order.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى تحتم تنجيته بلام الأمر عبارة عن معنى الخبر في قوله , عاجلا البحر كأنه ذو تمييز ليطيع الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shore is the bank of the Nile; ساحل is linked to water spreading or washing something to the side.
rows.anchor: أي شاطىء النيل , سمي ذلك لأن الماء يسحله , أي ينشره إلى جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who catches Moses is Pharaoh, called God's and Moses' enemy; he had slaughtered Israelite boys because of Moses.
rows.anchor: وهو المراد بقوله : { يأخذه } جوابا للأمر , أي موسى { عدو لي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the word enemy emphasizes the marvel that Pharaoh, who persecuted Israel for Moses' sake, would take Moses in and love him.
rows.anchor: ونبه على محل العجب بإعادة لفظ العدو في قوله : { وعدو له }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The love bestowed on Moses was immense; God made everyone who saw him love him because of his excellent character, preparing him for his mission.
rows.anchor: ليحبك كل من رآك لما جبلتك عليه من الخلال الحميدة , والشيم السديدة , لتكون أهلا لما أريدك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being raised under God's eye means easy upbringing by an ever-present caretaker, with God protecting him openly and attentively.
rows.anchor: وأنا حافظ لك حفظ من يلاحظ الشيء بعينه لا يغيب عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh loved Moses and searched widely for a nurse when he rejected the others; these events fulfilled God's plan and constrained Pharaoh, displaying the precise ordering of causes.
rows.anchor: فلما رآك هذا العدو أحبك وطلب لك المراضع , فلما لم تقبل واحدة منهن بالغ في الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' sister walked to where the family had left him to seek a nurse and asked Pharaoh's people whether she could direct them to a caregiver.
rows.anchor: أي في الموضع الذي وضعوك به لينظروا لك مرضعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her suggestion brought their mother, whose breast Moses accepted, returning him to her care.
rows.anchor: فقالوا : نعم ! فجاءت بأمك فقبلت ثديها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' return let his mother raise him safely and openly, cooling her eyes and ending her grief at separation and inability to care for him.
rows.anchor: حين دلتهم عليها { كي تقر } أي تبرد وتسكن { عينها } وتربيك آمنة عليك غير خائفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a grown man Moses killed an Egyptian while defending one of his own people, after which the Egyptians sought him to kill him.
rows.anchor: بعد أن صرت رجلا من القبط دفعا عن رجل من قومك فطلبت بها وأرادوا قتلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Moses from the anguish of fearing retribution for the killing by sending him as an emigrant toward Midian.
rows.anchor: بأن أخرجناك مهاجرا لديارهم نحو مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated trials were successive tests and rescues: birth during the killings, the river, nursing, Pharaoh's beard, the coal, the Egyptian's death, flight, service, losing the road, and scattered sheep at night.
rows.anchor: إذن الفتون ولادته عام الذبح وإبقاؤه في البحر ثم منعه الرضاع من غير ثدي أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Futūn may be a plural of fitna or fitna, with the tāʾ omitted, or a verbal noun on the pattern of shukūr.
rows.anchor: على أنه جمع فتن أو فتنة , على ترك الاعتداء بالتاء , ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا كالشكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses spent many years in Midian with the prophet Shuʿayb, learning his manners and marrying his daughter.
rows.anchor: مقيما عند نبينا شعيب عليه السلام يربيك بآدابه , وصاهرته على ابنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses arrived at the divinely appointed time, after reaching maturity, neither early nor late, to receive God's speech and be sent to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وقت قدرته في الأزل لتكليمي لك , وهو بلوغ الأشد والاستواء , وإرسالك إلى فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' mission to Pharaoh would carry out God's decree against the ruler who had killed Israelite sons out of fear of him.
rows.anchor: لأمضي فيه قدري الذي ذبح أبناء بني اسرائيل خوفا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's making Moses for Himself means raising him through acts of kindness as one deliberately formed for a purpose.
rows.anchor: ربيّتك بصنائع المعروف تربية من يتكلف تكوين المربى على طريقة من الطرائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose was that Moses implement God's laws and commands as an exclusive servant; the wording represents his nearness and honor.
rows.anchor: فهو تمثيل لما حوله من منزلة التقريب والتكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed command repeats the earlier order, grants Moses the brother he requested, and sends them with the signs God showed him and further signs displayed through him.
rows.anchor: كما تقدم أمري لك به { اخوك } كما سألت { بلآيتي } التي أريتك وغيرها مما أظهره على يديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition means not to grow weak or slacken.
rows.anchor: أي تفترا وتضعفا { في ذكري * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance encompasses their whole mission, and they must pursue it intensely with full attention of heart because this best serves their purpose; Moses had made it the goal of his prayer.
rows.anchor: في غاية الاجتهاد فبه وإحضار القلب له , فإن ذلك أعون شيء على المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warns them not to invent claims against God by calling His established signs unreal magic, presenting illusion as truth, or associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: لا تتعمدوا أن تصنعوا استعلاء { على الله كذبا } بحعلكم آياته العظام الثابتة سحرا لا حقيقة له

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the root sense of يسحت is to exterminate completely.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي . وأصله الاستئصال { بعذاب } أي عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who deliberately lies against God or anyone else is disappointed and ruined.
rows.anchor: كل { من افترى * } اي تعمد كذبا على الله أو على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers disputed after hearing Moses because they recognized that no one could address Pharaoh before his army in this way unless God supported him.
rows.anchor: علما منهم بأنه لا يقدر أن يواجه فرعون بمثله في جميع جنوده وأتباعه لم يسلم منه غلا من اللله معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They whispered to hide their disagreement from Pharaoh and his followers, lest their differences be exposed.
rows.anchor: وبالغوا في إخفائه , فإن النجوى الإسرار , لئلا يظهر فرعون وأتباعه على عوراهم في اختلافهم

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: After deliberating, the sorcerers adopted Pharaoh's insinuation to win his favor and turn people against Moses and Aaron, hoping to block their followers even if they prevailed, since one sorcerer can beat another.
rows.anchor: أي السحرة بعد النظر وإجالة الرأي ما خيلهم به فرعون تلقنا منه وتقربا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men called sorcerers are Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: إن هاذان } أي موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: The reading هاذان with alif keeps the dual alif in every case, a dialect attributed to several Arab tribes, including Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb and groups from Kināna, Khathʿam, Zubayd, Banū al-ʿAnbar, Banū al-Hujaym, Murād, and ʿUdhr.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وهي لغة لطوائف من العرب لبني الحارث بن كعب وبعض كنانة خثعم وزبيد

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: They claim Moses and Aaron intend to expel the Egyptians from their ancestral homeland with magic.
rows.anchor: يريدان } أي بما يقولان من دعوى الرسالة وغيرها { أن يخرجاكم } أيها الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their exemplary way refers to their magical tradition and, by extension, their religion, status, and livelihood, which they fear Moses and Aaron will eclipse.
rows.anchor: هذه السحرية التي تعبتم في تمهيدها , وأفنى فيها أسلافكم أعمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urge the sorcerers to bring every device they have and avoid division, which would weaken them.
rows.anchor: أي لا تدعوا منه شيئا إلا جئتم به ولا تختلفوا تضعفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should meet Moses and Aaron in a coordinated line, evenly matched and competing together; the formation would impress and intimidate spectators.
rows.anchor: متسابقين متساوين في السباق ليستعلي أمركم عليهما فتفلحوا , والصطفاف أهيب في صدور الرائين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful one is whoever prevails and establishes superiority in this contest.
rows.anchor: اي غلب ووجد علوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers use gentle speech to address their opponent, since courtesy can do no harm even if it does no good.
rows.anchor: لأن لين القول مع الخصم إن لم ينفع لم يضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their phrasing revealed that they preferred to cast first; Moses noticed and yielded so that his miracle would come last and leave no doubt.
rows.anchor: لأنه فهم أن مرادهم الابتداء , وليكون هو الآخر فيكون العاقبة بتسليط معجرته على سحرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ropes and staffs only seemed to move because of the extraordinary magic in which the sorcerers surpassed the people of the earth.
rows.anchor: التي ألقوها { يخيل إليه } وهو صفينا تخييلا مبتدئا { من سحرهم } الذي كانوا قد فاقوا به أهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajis is a thought or inward impression that Moses experienced privately because of the sight.
rows.anchor: وحقيقته : أوقع واجسا اي خاطرا وضميرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in himself is placed before Moses' fear to emphasize that the feeling was specifically his, not someone else's; نفس evokes ordinary human nature rather than the heart.
rows.anchor: كان المقام للاهتمام بتقديم المتعلق , فقال لذلك لا لمراعاة الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' fear resembles his earlier natural fear when he first saw his staff transform, and is presented as a human response.
rows.anchor: مثل ما خاف من عصاه أول ما رآها كذلك على ما هو طبع البشر

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: The sorcerers refuse to follow Pharaoh to escape his temporary punishment, choosing instead the clear signs Moses brought, which they witnessed and knew could not be matched.
rows.anchor: على ما جاءنا } به موسى عليه السلام { من البينات } التي عايناها وعلمنا أنه لا يقدر أحد على مضاهاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having inferred the Creator from the miraculous act, they name Him directly as the one who originated them, affirming His lordship over them, Pharaoh, and everyone else, and Pharaoh's helplessness.
rows.anchor: ترقوا إلى ذكره بعد معرفته بفعله , إشارة إلى علي قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do what he judges, recognizing that whatever he can do to them is only by God's permission.
rows.anchor: علما بأن ما فعله فهو بإذن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's rule reaches only the body and this short worldly life; the spirit faces lasting divine reward or punishment, so they fear only the One who judges beyond bodily death.
rows.anchor: إنما حكمك في مدتها على الجسد خاصة , فهي ساعة تعقب راحة , ةنحن لانخاف إلاممن يحكم على الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition في is omitted before this worldly life; even if Pharaoh's jurisdiction lasted to the world's end, it would remain fleeting beside God's enduring judgment.
rows.anchor: ولعلمه أسقطوا الجار تنزلا إلى أن حكمه لو فرض أنه يمتد إلى آخر الدنيا لكان أهلا لأن لا يخشى

words: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They trust their Lord, who cared for them throughout their lives despite their disbelief, and seek forgiveness without implying that their faith benefits or harms God.
rows.anchor: المحسن إلينا طول أعمارنا مع إساءتنا بالكفر وغيره

rows.speaker: السحرة
rows.claim: They single out the magic they were compelled to perform to counter the miracle; resisting Pharaoh would have been more fitting because God deserves greater reverence.
rows.anchor: لتعارض به المعجزة , فإن كان الأكمل لنا عصيانك فيه لأن الله أحق بأن يتقى

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: One report says that only two of Pharaoh's sorcerers were Copts; the rest were Israelites whom Pharaoh forced to learn magic.
rows.anchor: روي أم الذي كان من القبط من السحرة اثنان فقط , والباقون من بني إسرائيل أكرههم فرعون على تعلم السحر

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: Another report says the sorcerers saw Moses asleep while his staff guarded him and told Pharaoh that a sleeping magician's magic would fail; Pharaoh rejected this and forced them to compete.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم رأوا موسى عليه السلام نائما وعصاه تحرسه فقالوا لفرعون إن الساحر إذا نام بطل سحره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is better than Pharaoh in the reward He promises and more enduring in both reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: خير } جزاء منك فيما وعدتنا به { وأبقى * } ثوابا وعقابا

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the apparent outcome is that God saved the sorcerers from Pharaoh; the author supports this with Qur'an 28:35 and says the end of al-Hadid is explicit about their rescue.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الله تعالى سلمهم من فرعون , ويؤيده قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A criminal is one who breaks what God commanded him to uphold; he faces Hell, the abode of humiliation.
rows.anchor: أي قاطعا ما أمره به أن يوصل { فإن له جهنم } دار الإهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinner never dies despite the severity of Hell; Pharaoh's punishment, by contrast, would either kill quickly if severe or end in death if mild.
rows.anchor: لا يموت فيها } أبدا مع شدة عذابها . بخلاف عذابك الذي إن اشتد أمات فزال سريعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned person has no life in Hell from which he can benefit.
rows.anchor: ولا يحيى * } فيها حياة ينتفع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is accompanied and confirmed by righteous deeds; true faith implies that its possessor acts righteously.
rows.anchor: فكأن صادق الإيمان مستلزم لصالح الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers receive exalted ranks incomparable with the ranks Pharaoh had promised the sorcerers.
rows.anchor: التي لا نسبة لدرجاتك التي وعدتنا بها منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gardens of Eden are prepared for permanent residence, with the conditions for dwelling already provided.
rows.anchor: أعدت للإقامة وهيئت فيها أسبابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rivers flow beneath the gardens' rooms, beds, and grounds; wherever a river is desired, one flows.
rows.anchor: أي من تحت غرفها وأسرتها وأرضها ؛ فلا يراد موضع منها لأن يجري فيه نهر إلا جرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the gardens, like the gardens themselves, are prepared for permanent residence.
rows.anchor: أن أهلها هيئوا أيضا للإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax supplies an omitted antecedent: that immense lasting bliss is the reward of those who purified themselves through faith and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: أن التقدير : ذلك الجزاء العظيم والنعيم المقيم جزاء الموصوفين , لتزكيتهم أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This promise consoles the Companions for the persecution they faced when the sūra was revealed.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا تسلية للصحابة رضوان الله عليهم فيما كان يفعل بهم عند نزول هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This majestic form of revelation brings glad tidings, ease, warning, disclosure, and eloquent arrangement; the Arabic Qur'an gathers intended meanings and makes them clear to those who know Arab styles.
rows.anchor: أنزلناها على هذا المنوال العزيز المثال { وكذلك } أي ومثل هذا الإنزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God repeats the warnings while varying their forms and arranging diverse styles together.
rows.anchor: ذكرناه مكررين له محولا في أساليب مختلفة , وأفانين متنوعة مؤتلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aim is that readers may be led to fear God and sustain taqwa as a lasting habit, protecting themselves from what they fear.
rows.anchor: بأن تكون له وصفا مستمرا , وهي الحذر الحامل على اتخاذ الوقاية مما يحذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The varied warnings may renew their awareness of paths to good and awaken fear that turns them from base desires and distress.
rows.anchor: ما يستحق أن يذكر من طرق الخير , فيكون سببا للخوف الحامل على التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verses reach the height of eloquence and wisdom, displaying complete knowledge, power, and justice; after exalting His book, God exalts Himself to teach servants His due.
rows.anchor: دالة على أن لقائلها تمام العلم والقدرة والعدل ف أحوال الدراين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's transcendence exceeds what describers can fully express or intellects can encompass, and is untouched by the false descriptions of deniers and polytheists.
rows.anchor: بلغ الذي لا يبلغ الواصفون وصفه حق وصفه من العلو أمرا لاتحتمله العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the King whom nothing can overcome and the only true sovereign; His kingship is real and never passes away.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يعجزه شيء , فلا ملك في الحقيقة غيره { الحق } اي الثابت الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, the command not to turn away from the remembrance is followed by a warning not to rush ahead by reciting the Qur'an before its revelation is complete.
rows.anchor: فلا تعرض عنه , بل أقبل عليه لتكون من المتقين الذاكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here hastening with the Qur'an specifically means hastening its recitation.
rows.anchor: أي بتلاوته

words: مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase makes the prohibition cover all times before completion, while the passive construction focuses on revelation being completed rather than on a particular revealer.
rows.anchor: بنى للمجهول قوله : { يقضى } أي ينهى

words: مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not send the Qur'an all at once but in measured, successive revelation; the Prophet should listen attentively, then recite after it is complete.
rows.anchor: كما أنا لم نعجل بإنزاله عليك جملة , بل رتلناه لك ترتيلا , زنزلناه إليك تنزيلا مفصلا تفصيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks his nurturing Lord to deepen his understanding of what has been revealed and to reveal further knowledge, including knowledge that draws people to follow him.
rows.anchor: أي بتفهيم ما أنزلت إلي منه وإنزال غيره كما زدتني بإنزاله وتحفيظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Careful reflection and listening benefit learning more than haste and aid retention; what is fully understood is best preserved.
rows.anchor: أن التاني في العلم بالتدبر وبإلقاء السمع أنفع من الاستعجال المتعب للبال المكدر للحال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet prayed for benefit from learned knowledge, useful knowledge, increase in knowledge, praise in every condition, and refuge from the state of the people of Hell; al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and al-Bazzar transmit it, with no grading stated here.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Moses story displays God's patience with servants who forget covenants; after praising the Reminder, condemning those who turn away, and instructing the Prophet about it, the sūra turns to Adam to warn against forgetfulness and urge repentance, showing God's ancient practice of forbearance toward inherently deficient people.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك سبحانه قصة آدم عليه السلام تحذيرا من الركون إلى ما يسبب النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqai connects the verse either with the earlier statement that God sent down an Arabic judgment (13:37) or with the promise to recount past histories, reaffirming the Qur'anic instruction and fulfilling that promise.
rows.anchor: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's earlier covenant with Adam, the father of humanity, prohibited eating from the tree; Adam forgot it and ate despite knowing God's majesty.
rows.anchor: أبي البشر الذي أطلعناه على كثير منها في النهي عن الأكل من الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Adam held an exalted rank, his lapse was counted as a sin, following the maxim that the good deeds of the righteous are the faults of those brought near.
rows.anchor: فعددنا عليه وقوعه في ذلك المنهي ناسيا ذنبا لعلو رتبته عندنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam lacked a firm, decisive purpose and unwavering will of the sort attributed to angels; God did not know such resolve to be present in him.
rows.anchor: أي قصدا صلبا ماضيا وإرادة نافذة لا تردد فيها كإرادات الملائكة عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the lapse, God forgave Adam and did not remove him from the rank of the chosen.
rows.anchor: ومع ذلك عفونا عنه ولم نزحوحه عن رتبة الاصطفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's purpose is to show God's forbearance toward those who stray and His power over rejecters; Adam's failure is first summarized and then detailed, naming it disobedience to warn against forbidden acts and direct the deficient toward prompt repentance.
rows.anchor: ذكر فعله آدم عليه السلام هذه في هذه السورة بلفظ المعصية مع التصريح بأنها وجه النسيان , وذكر ذلك أولا مجملا ثم أتبعه تفصيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are described as naturally decisive and resolute, without hesitation or slackness.
rows.anchor: المجبولين على مضي العزم والتصميم على القصد من غير مانع تردد ولا عائع فتور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded the angels to prostrate only after choosing Adam, already knowing what would happen; Adam's later lapse does not undo his election because divine clemency and mercy allow the erring to return.
rows.anchor: لم نأمرهم بذلك إلا بعد أن اصطفيناه ونحن عالمون بما سيقع منه , وأنه لا يقدح في رتبة اصطفائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis refused out of arrogance, attributing injustice and lack of wisdom to God; he disbelieved, despaired of mercy, lost goodness, and persisted in misleading creatures through deception.
rows.anchor: الذي نسب الله إلى الجور والإخلال بالحكمة فكفر فايس من الرحمة وسلب الخير فأصر على إضلال الخلق بالتلبيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis' pride toward Adam arose from envy and would not disappear; Eve is included as Adam's wife because she is from him.
rows.anchor: الشيطان الذي تكبر عليك { عدو لك } دائما لأن لبكبر الناشىء عن الحسد لا يزول { ولزوجك } لأنها منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is directed to Satan while its intended protection is for Adam and his wife; it spares her a direct prohibition, and assigning the expulsion to Satan intensifies the warning.
rows.anchor: وجه النهي إليه والمراد : هما , تنبيها على أن لها من الجلالة ما ينبغي أن تصان عن أن يتوجه إليها نهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God warns that Satan will persist in seeking their harm and removal from the Garden.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يقصر في ضركما وإرادة إنزالكما عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Eve shares the expulsion and its effects, the verse singles out Adam's toil because the author sees the man as responsible for labor, protection, and care, especially for his wife; an upright husband guides her to good, while a corrupt one leads her to harm.
rows.anchor: وكان أغلب تعبه في أمر المرأة , أفرد لاتحذير منه
